records.statement: A generated consumer repository must have the full sc-lint toolchain installed.
records.scope: the c-2 generated-consumer lint sprint and any plan item that edits template sc-lint setup or default or full lint commands
records.check: A generated fixture runs just setup, ordinary just lint, and named default and full profiles while its receipt records sc-boundary, sc-portability, and sc-runtime.

pass: Consumer setup installs the full sc-lint toolchain, including its boundary, portability, and runtime analyzers.
fail: Consumer setup installs only rustfmt and clippy and does not install the sc-lint toolchain.

records.quote: a full sc-lint is installed on a consumer repo

records.statement: Phase C must upgrade rmcp and utoipa to their latest released versions.
records.scope: the c-1 compatibility contract and c-3 runtime ecosystem upgrade sprints
records.check: Cargo metadata for the runtime and generated daemon composition graph reports one reachable package identity for rmcp, utoipa, and utoipa-axum.

pass: Phase C checks the released rmcp and utoipa versions and upgrades both dependencies to the latest releases.
fail: Phase C keeps the older rmcp and utoipa dependencies despite newer released versions being available.

records.quote: upgrading rmcp/utopia to the latest releave version should be planned in phase-<next>

records.statement: The repository and generated template must both use sc-lint 0.8.4.
records.scope: the c-1 consumer contract and c-2 template lint profile sprints
records.check: The root and template sc-lint configuration require 0.8.4, and each bootstrap path installs or verifies that version.

pass: Both the repository and generated template declare sc-lint 0.8.4 and their bootstrap commands install or verify 0.8.4.
fail: The repository bootstraps sc-lint 0.8.4 while the generated template declares and installs 0.8.0.

records.quote: both repo and templates should use 0.8.4

records.statement: The current phase must be named phase-c.
records.scope: every Phase C plan item and its plan metadata
records.check: A targeted repository scan of Phase C assets reports no phase-bc, bc-<n>, or ARCH-BC identifiers.

pass: Plan documents live under docs/plans/phase-c, sprint IDs are c-1 through c-4, and current branch, triage, and QA metadata use phase-c.
fail: The current plan, sprint IDs, branch metadata, triage, and QA evidence still use phase-bc and bc-1 through bc-4.

records.statement: Phase C planning must use a dedicated worktree and a separate pull request to develop.
records.scope: the Phase C plan branch, worktree, and pull request metadata
records.check: Git worktree metadata records plan/phase-c separately, and its pull request targets develop.

pass: Git worktree metadata shows a separate plan/phase-c checkout, and its dedicated planning pull request targets develop.
fail: Phase C planning is committed directly on the primary develop checkout and has no separate planning pull request.

records.quote: planning should be done on a second pr to develop on a dedicated $sc-git-worktree

records.statement: Phase C must keep rusqlite on the 0.39 release line.
records.scope: the c-3 runtime ecosystem upgrade sprint and any plan item that changes Cargo dependency versions for rusqlite, sqlx, or libsqlite3-sys
records.check: Cargo metadata and the SQLite resolver test show rusqlite 0.39.x and libsqlite3-sys 0.37 with no libsqlite3-sys 0.38.

pass: Phase C retains rusqlite 0.39.x while upgrading the other approved dependencies.
fail: Phase C upgrades rusqlite from 0.39 to a newer minor release line.

records.quote: so rusqlite will remain at 0.39? I will have beads-cache downgrade so everything is consistent.

records.statement: Fresh consumer installation must generate a default boundaries policy selected from the consumer's configuration settings.
records.scope: c-1 consumer policy contract and c-2 fresh-install implementation
records.check: Generate supported consumer configurations and verify their emitted policy matches selected crates and edges.

pass: Fresh consumer installation reads the selected configuration and generates the matching default boundaries policy before running sc-boundary.
fail: Fresh consumer installation emits no boundaries policy and runs sc-boundary only in no-manifest mode, regardless of configuration.

records.quote:
and you will need to determine the 'appropriate' default policy to install on consumer repos
based on configuration settings

records.statement: After fresh setup, the generated boundaries policy must be owned by the consumer repository.
records.scope: c-1 consumer policy ownership contract and c-2 generated policy handoff
records.check: Generated policy lives in the consumer repository and documented setup identifies the consumer as owner.

pass: Fresh setup writes the initial boundaries policy into the consumer repository and documents that the consumer owns subsequent policy decisions.
fail: The generated consumer's boundaries policy remains centrally owned by sc-runtime, which decides all subsequent consumer boundary changes.

records.quote: you will need to generate a boundaries policy for a 'fresh install' once a consumer is set up, they will have their own boundaries policy
